utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Two people on their feet. I'll start with my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have a preliminary matter to raise and it ought to be in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Your Honours, it's a brief matter. As you know, the Prosecution engage in proofing witnesses and they are, of course, today going to submit a reply to the motion or the draft motion of my learned friend Mr. Topolski. This witness was interviewed by the Prosecution in 2003. At that time, he was shown a photo line-up which included the picture of my client, Mr. Limaj. At that time, being shown those photographs by Mr. Lehtinen, the witness stated that he could not identify Mr. Limaj as having anything to do with the camp at all. And that was right after, of course, he had relived his experience at the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't mean -- I'm sorry to interrupt. My view is that is not exactly -- that is not an accurate reflection of what the witness said when he looked at the line-up, but I don't think we need to go into that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it will all come out in the wash, of course. The witness in fact said that the person looks familiar, in 2003, but I don't recognise him from the camp at all. That was the thrust of it, but that will come out. My point is somewhat different. The Prosecution have very courteously informed me, upon my request, that the witness arrived in The Hague on Saturday, the 27th of November. And he has spoken to the Prosecution a number of times on Saturday, Sunday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. On the Sunday, so the second time he met the Prosecution, not at the first meeting, the witness says that in 1999 he happened to be surfing on the Internet and he came across a small -- well, he came across a picture which he identifies as being the man who released him at the camp. Your Honour, that picture will be shown to you no doubt in the Prosecution's examination-in-chief. In fact, it's part of the video. It's a captured still from part of the video that was shown in open session. Perhaps Your Honours will remember the portion. It's when my learned friend Mr. Topolski turned to and said the person sitting next to Mr. Limaj, standing next to Mr. Limaj at the head of this parade was Mr. Musliu. So it was broadcast in open session. The difficulty I've got because of the late disclosure on the 1st of December, just a couple of days ago, is that I have not been able and we have not been able to make the necessary investigations as to the provenance of both the still captured on the Internet that the witness says he saw. And in particular we have not been able to investigate the basic issues; firstly, whether this Internet site, which is a Serb Internet site, www.Kosovo.com, whether or not that existed in 1999, because as Your Honours know, of course, Internet sites come and go. And secondly, if it did exist, we want to investigate what stills were on that site at that time, and that is possible. Now, Your Honours, the Prosecution, of course, have far more resources than us. I know my friend Mr. Nicholls is not aware of anybody in the office having that speciality, but I'm very happy for the Prosecution to make those inquiries and let me know if that web site existed in 1999, and if so, what was on it. But if I can't find that information, it's going to be extremely difficult to pitch the cross-examination at this particular witness. So, Your Honour, the purpose of my rising is simply to give you and Your Honours notice or heads-up that it may be the case at a later stage, depending on how events pan out today, that I will not be a position to cross-examine, because the only cross-examination for this witness was focused on the new disclosure, which is identification. I didn't have any questions for the previous witness and I didn't intend to ask this witness any questions either. It's accepted, of course, that these witnesses have been through a lot and one does not want to drag them over the coals, as it were, so I want to know exactly what the state of play is in advance of asking particular questions. So it may be a case, Your Honours, that unless the Prosecution can provide me those two primary facts, as it were, I may at a later stage be asking for the matter -- or for the witness to stay over until at least Monday to give me a further opportunity, to give us a further opportunity of making what I submit are these very necessary and very fundamental investigations. Your Honour, that's the observation I make at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Mr. Nicholls, this seems to be a late disclosure issue. Are the Prosecution in a position to facilitate Mr. Khan's need for further information?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know that we are, Your Honour, and I oppose the motion to keep the witness longer for several reasons. First of all, whenever the witness may have first seen this photo, what happened is he didn't tell us about it until he arrived. He found it on the Internet here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not a matter of blame, it's a matter of the fairness of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I understand. What I'm trying to get to, Your Honour, is the piece of information he seeks I think is a bit peripheral, because whether the witness is correct that he saw it in 1999 or not, whether the web site was up in 1999 or not, he told us he saw a photo on the Internet, we asked him if he could find it, he found it, he showed it to us. That photo is on the Internet now. So at some point he saw that photo which he believes depicts what he said it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you say he found the photo, do you mean that he had a print of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No. He searched on a terminal and said, That's the one I'm talking about, and then it was printed off of the screen. I -- this issue was raised this morning. I don't know what -- I'm not a person who's got any expertise in web sites or when this is -- when these -- how these things can be tracked. My friend Colin Black has looked at the web site now and it says that on the cover it says copyright 1997, Kosovo.com, if that helps. However, all of the questions are entirely speculative, this need for recalling the witness. He can do his cross-examination as he would. The only issue he's not able to tell for certain is whether he, my friend, knows the date that the web site was up. But every other question he can ask. In the future he may discover that in fact it was up in 1999 and then that question is gone, there's no reason to ask it. And if it was not, if it was later, it's a fairly peripheral issue, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may appear peripheral from some viewpoints, but if, for example, it is true that that picture is now on a web site but that it has only very recently occurred, the effect upon credit could be significant, could it not? And we -- I put that as a hypothetical possibility because there's no way at the moment of knowing the fundamental facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, exactly -- that's exactly right, Your Honour. It is hypothetical, which is why I think at the moment that there isn't a problem. If there is a need to recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think our minds are not meeting, Mr. Nicholls. Whether there is a problem or not will not be known until it is discovered when this web site existed and whether this photo was on it at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The witness can answer that to the best of his recollection. We -- I will do what I can to find out the questions of when the web site existed and when the photo was up. I just have to say this morning I don't know how that is done and how soon it can be done. I will check with travel plans and see whether Monday is a problem. I don't think it will be, but I can check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment, unless you can assist Mr. Khan before then, I think you must anticipate the witness will need to be here on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Any further matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could remind you of the affirmation you took when you commenced your evidence, it still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls will continue to ask you questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, please take your time to listen carefully and understand the question. Take your time, as much time as you need, to answer. Now, when we left off last night we had just finished speaking about how you entered this camp compound through the gates and you indicated to the Trial Chamber that you were then led with the other people who had been in the van with you into a room in the main house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. We have guests with us this morning and the microphones aren't working. I'm sorry to interrupt. We'll get it fixed. There's no reason why Mr. Black [sic] can't proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're catching my disease, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Does Your Honour get better?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On odd days. I have good days, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: We've noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember we were talking about that stage of your journey?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, can you please describe as best you can from your memory the room which you were taken into in the house.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the main room there was a smallish corridor, with the toilet to the left. Inside, in the main room there were mattresses on the floor and there was some kind of a stove next to the radiators -- I'm sorry, next to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to now show the witness from P5. It will take one moment to come up. That's our visual presentation, an image.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the -- what is in the photo in front of you, which, for the record, is building A1 in our locations booklet.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where we were kept at the beginning, on the ground floor. That's where the main centre was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And for the record, this is from P6, it's A1. U008-3669. I would ask Mr. Younis if he can please show the interior of the ground floor. And if we could look around that room, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recognise what's being shown in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise the room, but everything that's in it wasn't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just for the record, that's a room which you were initially brought into?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'll also say just for the record that I started showing you that room earlier when you were here but we stopped before we looked at it. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who was in the room when you were brought into there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers. I'm not sure how many of them, but several.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what happened to you and your father? What happened after you were brought into the room? What is the first thing that you remember happening?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They made us sit on some mattresses and started to interrogate us; where we were from, what we were doing in Kosovo. And on the other side, they were beating Genov.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who was asking you these questions, if you remember anything in particular about the person who was asking you these questions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that there was any specific feature about this man, but I assume that he was one of the people in charge there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We'll talk about that in a moment. How long were you kept in this room with your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about an hour, an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what happened to Genov during that whole time? You started saying that he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They beat him with rifle butts, they kicked him; anything they could lay their hands on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about Cuk, Mr. Cuk?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you remember, did they, the soldiers who were beating Genov, give any reason of why they were doing that or did they ask him any questions while they were beating him?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They just referred to him as the Serbian police. As they were beating him, they were calling him the police and saying this is what the Serbian police is doing to the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you started saying that the person who was asking you questions seemed to be somebody in charge. Tell me why you thought this person was the person who was in charge. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he entered the room, everybody saluted him and stood at attention when he approached us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you please describe that man who everybody saluted as well as you can from your memory. And I'll give you some cues: How old did he appear to be?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his mid-30s, perhaps 35, 36.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How tall was he?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 180 to 185 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was his build? And by that I mean what was he like physically? Was he big? Thin? Just if you could describe his build.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was of medium build. He was not thin, he was not fat, he was medium build.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe his hair for us.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had longer -- slightly longer hair, combed back, with some gray in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did he have any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was clean-shaven, not freshly shaven, but he didn't have any facial hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you describe his uniform for us, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a camouflage uniform, just as everybody else had, but it was much neater and cleaner than the uniforms of the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did he directly ask you questions or were those questions directed to your father or to both of you? If you can describe the questioning a little bit from this man.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was directed to both of us because they knew that we were father and son, so the questions were directed to the two of us, not separately each one of us. The interrogation went along the lines of what we were doing at Kosovo, where we were going by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long did this questioning last?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10, 15 minutes, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how did this person you've described as the person in charge of the soldiers, when he was asking you and your father these questions, what was his demeanour like? How was he behaving towards you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was a very pleasant person. He never indicated that he wanted to hurt us in any way. He behaved in a very soldier-like fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was this person, this person in charge, present at the same time that Genov was being beaten in this room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As far as you could tell, what was his reaction to that beating, if any?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his reaction was along the lines that he was happy that they had caught him and happy that they were beating him. But he himself did not do anything. He stood back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And during this conversation you had with this man who was in charge, how far away from him were you? Were you both sitting or standing? If you can describe how you, your father, and this person were situated in the room.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He sat maybe about half a metre away from us. We were sitting on the floor, he sat across from us. The distance was perhaps half a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was he writing or taking any notes during this conversation or recording it in any way?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see this man, this person who was in charge of the soldiers, again before you ultimately left the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the first person to tell us that we would be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we'll talk about that again later on in a little more detail, but can you just tell us when that was and where that conversation took place.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. What do you mean by "conversation"? The first conversation or the second conversation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My fault, I'm sorry. The second conversation, or the subsequent conversation when he said -- told you that you were going to be released, when did that take place?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the room upstairs of the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were there any other times besides these two occasions that you spoke to this man in charge?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long did that second conversation or when he spoke to you and told you and your father you were going to be released, how long did that last?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not longer than 15 to 20 minutes. It was just -- the question was how we felt, whether everything was okay with us, and then he announced that we would be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And was his behaviour towards you the same as on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, after your release from this camp, did you ever see a picture of this man again?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where did you see the picture?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over the Internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When was that that you saw the picture on the Internet, as well as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been about a year after the events. When my family bought a computer, we were interested to see what was going on in Kosovo, and at a web site, we found their pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was the address of the web site?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Kosovo.com.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall when you first told people from my office about seeing that photo and recognising the person who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a few days ago. I think that you were the first person to whom I actually showed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were you able to go on an Internet terminal here and find the photo you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would now like to show the witness a photograph. It will be on Sanction; however, I've given the witness a hard copy. Unfortunately, Your Honour, this does not have an ERN number. I was unable to get it an ERN reference number before this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, could you look at the photo in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it may be more appropriate, in fact, rather than show a blow-up, to show the actual web page itself. That's what the witness identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what he has in front of him, Mr. Khan. It may be blown-up on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honours, if you've got the actual web page. It's considerably smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I can show the actual -- Your Honours have the photo which I'm showing to the witness. It is not the actual web page, I have the actual web page, but the only relevant portion is the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it may assist. I can hand mine up if it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have a page, I find --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- with a smaller version --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will -- perhaps you could clarify what size it was from the witness, as he recalls it, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: First of all, sir, you see the size of the photo in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is that the size of the photograph that you found on the Internet here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is that the same photograph which you found here in The Hague that you were looking at in 1999 when you recognised the person in charge at the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the same picture that I saw here in The Hague, but in 1999 it was -- the picture was much larger and that was not the only picture there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Other than the difference in size of the picture, is there any other difference between the picture you saw in 1999 and the picture which you found here and which is before you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No difference, except that it is much more difficult to see it, to discern the faces here in this photograph. Other than that, it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why is it more difficult here? Is that because of the size or any other reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I would ask my friend be careful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm just trying to be clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is because of the size of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If the witness could be given a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to just, perhaps from the bottom of the photo, draw an arrow pointing, if you can, exactly to the person in the photo which you've been referring to as the one you recognised on the web site in 1999.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you can do that on the photo which is to your left on that machine -- oh, I'm sorry. I didn't see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd ask that that be admitted, Your Honour. I think it's P80.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P80.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it may seem like a small point, I don't know at the moment, but I would ask that perhaps once again - it's a very simple exercise - but the actual page from the Internet that the witness saw, the whole page be put before him and he can just do the arrow on that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you want that in as well, Mr. Khan, you may do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. I don't know at the moment where it's going, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, in cross-examination, not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you gave a statement to an ICTY investigator in January 2003. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And over time you've had several contacts with an investigator from this office about logistical matters, including the time of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to request that you be careful, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just be careful, Mr. Nicholls. I know you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you had contact with investigators from the ICTY subsequent to your statement in 2003?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just regarding our arrival here. That was over the past few months.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you, if you can, tell the Court why you didn't tell the investigator in 2003 about having seen the photograph which has just been marked an exhibit and did not let us know until you arrived here recently.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, really. I thought that it was not that important. Since it was on the Internet, it was in public access. I thought you knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd now like to show the witness a short video clip. It's P35, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we can back up just a tiny bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And -- sorry -- okay. That's enough. We can remove that from the screen. I have a still from that video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recognise anything from that video clip? And I should say that you were shown that video clip earlier, when you arrived here, after you talked about the photograph.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did recognise the man who told us that we would be set free.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'd now like to give the still from that exhibit to the witness. If that can be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just mention now that of course the video that was shown to the witness of course mentions the name Fatmir Limaj. I just raise that, obviously for your attention at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'll ask you, Witness: When you were shown that video in -- before, here, did it have any writing or sound? Was there any of that captioning underneath that you saw?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't think there were any captions. I didn't really pay any attention, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like you to, if you could, in the same way mark the still to the left of you with a pen. Please mark the person who you just said you recognised as the -- it's off the screen -- you said as the person who told you you would be set free; the same person from the other photo.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to move that into evidence as P81, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P81.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, I want to keep talking back to where we were, about what was going on in that room, the first room you were brought into where you were questioned. Out of the other soldiers present there, did you learn the names or nicknames of any of them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of them, who later brought us food and other supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was he doing in the room during the events you've described, during the questioning and during the beating of Genov? What was he doing there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not sure. I didn't pay attention to individuals at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you say that he brought you food and other supplies. How often during your stay in the camp did you see this man again, Shala?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How did he treat you when you had contact with him?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The same thing -- the same questions that I asked you about the commander, can you tell me as best you can what you remember of Shala's appearance at that time. You can start with what you think his age was --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You can -- excuse me. I would at this point ask that -- the question is self-evident. He does not need to lead him through a description with suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I don't think asking what his age was is a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm concerned about what is about to come, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Continue to prompt attention to specific features, if you think that will help, Mr. Nicholls, but not the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think I got anywhere near suggesting the answer, but I'll go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You keep wanting to justify yourself, Mr. Nicholls. You've been given the green light. Take it before I change my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you please describe Shala as you remember him, how he appeared in 1998.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was of medium height, an older man with a moustache, good-natured.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how did you come to leave that room in the house, the room where you were first brought and questioned?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were talking amongst themselves and at one point they told us to get up and that they were taking us elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just as a follow-up for that, who was talking among themselves, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the soldiers, among themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened? Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us to the basement of the house that was next to this headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you told at this time how long you were going to be held while you were being put in this basement? Anything -- any information along those lines?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't tell us anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who went with you to this basement? Did that -- can you tell us who was put in the basement besides yourself.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, my father, Cuk, and they carried Genov to the basement, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could have -- give the witness back P79, please, and that's the one which we all have a hard copy which doesn't need to be displayed. It's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, it's actually pretty self-evident from this diagram, but can you tell the Court just by number and what is written which -- where the basement was that you were brought to.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between number 2A and toilet 2. The word is in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you've -- and -- okay. Thank you. And you've labelled the location "basement." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, have you ever drawn or diagrammed that basement room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interior of the basement, you mean, with the rest?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when did you do that diagram?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2003, when the investigator came to visit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Before you drew that diagram, were you shown any pictures, sketches, anything by the investigator of the -- of that room that you diagrammed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to now show the witness U003-2188. Your Honours, for the same reasons as P79, I'd ask that we just look at that in hard copy and not broadcast it. Does everybody have that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document that's before you, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, underneath the date on the right-hand side, in the upper portion of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And is this the sketch which you've been telling us that you drew?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just to be very clear, did you personally draw -- I'm not talking about the writing, but all of the drawing here of the diagram, did you draw all of those lines or just some of them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the numbers and where our names are written, I did all that. As for the square around everything, I'm not sure whether I drew it or the investigator, but the door, the windows, I drew all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, looking at the diagram, could you please explain to us as much as you remember, and you can use the diagram, what this room was like, and I mean the dimensions and what the different items you've marked in the room are.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the room was very small. It was, say, 2 metres by 4 or 3 by 4 -- 2 by 4, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you've indicated that there was -- can you explain what -- this is where you've indicated on the left and you've written that there was a shelf.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some kind of a shelf was there. Perhaps 40 centimetres up from the floor, and its length could have been about 30 or 40 centimetres. That's how wide it was, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you've drawn two circles on the bottom left and one of them is labelled "bucket." Can you tell us clearly what those two circles represent.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That bucket was our toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what is the smaller circle next to the bucket? What was that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was some kind of drainage. I think it was a kind of toilet, too, because we used that as a toilet as well. We used the bucket to pass stool.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to now show the witness P5.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Would you look at that image, sir, and tell me if you recognise that.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recognise it. That's the entrance into the basement and the basement window.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: For the record, from our location booklet, P6, that is room A5, U008-3676. Mr. Younis, if we could look at the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Would you look at that picture, sir, the same exhibit, U008-3677. Tell me if you recognise that photo.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basement is where we were, but none of these things were inside. The refrigerator wasn't there and all of these things that are on the left-hand side. It was just an empty room with hay on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The last photo, the next photo, same exhibit, U008-3678. I'd ask you to look at that picture and tell us if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My father and I sat and slept in that corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just for the record, could you -- you've indicated on your diagram, which we'll look at later, but could you tell us which corner you mean by "that corner." If you could describe it.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that corner on the right-hand side where the man is standing. That's where my father slept by the wall, and I slept next to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when the four of you were brought into this room you started telling us about, was there anybody else in the room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were a few more people in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember how many people were in the room when you were brought in there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure at this point in time whether it was six or seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you -- and what kind of people were these in the room? Who were they, what sort of people?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, that and were these guards or soldiers or what kind of people were they?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were prisoners. There were three Albanians and four Serbs -- three or four Serbs, prisoners, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember the names or nicknames of any of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I never found out until only recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could the witness please be given back this sketch under seal. I've forgotten the exhibit number. No, sorry, not that one. The most recent one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I suspect you may mean a document that has not yet been put in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you wish to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll perhaps ask him a few more questions and then seek to tender it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, you're now looking at U003-2188, the sketch you drew of the interior of the basement room where you were held prisoner. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, around the perimeter from the top of the drawing and down the right-hand side, you've drawn some oval shapes and written some words next to them and some numbers. Can you tell us what these represent, what you were drawing here. You could start maybe at the top left.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are drawings of people, where they were in that basement, where they sat or where they slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Please continue, sorry.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the upper left-hand side, there were three Albanian men. They sat there, and then my father and I and the rest. As you can see, it was Genov, Cuk, and the four other men whose names I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now tender that under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P82 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While you were in this prison with the other men -- the other prisoners you've indicated on your diagram, were you able to speak with any of the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were not allowed to talk at all. But we did whisper and talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you overhear any conversations between other prisoners who might have been whispering to each other?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really. I didn't pay attention, but they did talk among themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, do you remember when you gave your statement in January 2003 whether you were shown any photos that you identified?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were any of those photos that you identified of people -- well, where were these -- who were the people in the photos you identified, focusing now on the area of testimony we're talking about, the prison.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator brought me some pictures, and in them I identified the other prisoners -- well, not all of them but most of the prisoners who were in that basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I showed you some of those same photos after you arrived here. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a photo now, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is from P54, which is under seal; however, this photo can be displayed. It's U003-2164.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I recognise that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We've already done that one. You've identified that person earlier in your testimony. I should have said 2166. Do you recognise the person in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What can you -- where do you recognise him from?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was one of the people in the basement. Later on, we heard from him that the vehicle they used to bring us to the camp and to the school had originally been seized from him, that it was his vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you just describe that conversation a little bit more, how you learned that it was the same vehicle.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he asked us where they caught us and how they brought us in. We said that it was on the road to Prizren. And he asked us how it happened, and we said that we were brought to a school, in a Golf car. And he asked what kind of a Golf, and we said it was navy blue. And he said, Yes, that's my Golf. They took me in that Golf and they away that car of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember if you discussed any other features of the car, other than its make and colour?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What was discussed were the Swiss licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything else that you remember about this man? You've said you don't remember the names, but where he was from, perhaps, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that he and another man were going through Prizren and they stopped them. This other man was also in the camp or in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd now like to show you another photo. The same exhibit number U003-2168. Take a moment to look at that picture and let me know if you recognise the person in it.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise him. He was with us in the basement. He had a bullet hole in his leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is there anything else you remember about this man; where he was from, how he'd come to be in the basement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he just told me that he had been on a bus, trying to -- that he was trying to escape and that they shot at him and hit him in the leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then finally I'd like to show you another photo. P54 again, U003-2169. Can you tell me if you recognise the man in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This man and the man from the first picture that you showed me were together, they were travelling together in that Golf car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Anything else you remember about this man, other than what you've told us?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was always smiling. Somehow he could make everybody smile all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm finished with that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you had drawn where people were in the room. Did people stay in the same places -- sorry. First of all, how long -- how many days and nights did you spend in this room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about five -- three or five nights. I'm not sure at this time. I think it was about five nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did the people who you've shown where they stayed in this room, did they stay in the same places during that time or did people -- were people able to move around in the room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people would perhaps move for a few minutes, but everybody had to sit in their places, otherwise they would be beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what about Genov? Was he able to move around at all when he was in this room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was unable to move. I'm not sure, but something was broken, either his leg or his back. But at any rate, he was unable to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to describe as well as you can remember what the conditions in the room were like for you and the other prisoners during the time that you spent there. First of all, what was the temperature like in that room? How hot or cold was it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The temperature was very high. It was hot. Since it was July, it was very hot in the room because there were no openings. There was just a small window. The area was very small and there were many people in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was the air like in that room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very bad, since we had to relieve ourselves, sleep, and eat in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You started talking about the floor earlier and talked about some hay on it. Can you remember what the floor was made out of?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a concrete floor with more water than cement in it. It was very wet. The floor was very wet. It was probably also due to some pipes that were broken inside the wall, and there was straw thrown all over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "due to some pipes that were broken inside the wall"? Can you just describe what that has to do with the floor being wet a little more.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the wall behind my father and myself there was a leak. Water was leaking in the very corner. I think that plumbing, a pipe in the wall had been broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's clear. What did you and the other prisoners sleep on in that room? Were you provided with any kind of bedding, blankets, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing. We used our own shoes as cushions, as pillows, but otherwise we slept on the hay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you describe what food you were provided with during the time you were in the basement room.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't describe the food. It's impossible to describe. I'm not sure if there was any meat in it. There was some kind of a soup made of all kinds of things. I cannot really tell you what it was made of. It looked more like animal fodder than anything that was fit for humans.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how often were you provided with this food?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what about water for drinking; how was that given to you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every person received a bottle of water and that would be filled once a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you -- were you able to smoke -- or did you smoke in this room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were more cigarettes than we could smoke. We would be given cigarettes two or three times a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you started, when you were describing your diagram, to talk about the bucket that was used as a toilet. Did everybody in the prison, in that room with you, use the same bucket? Was there just one bucket?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the only bucket that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How often was that bucket emptied?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you -- what about, now, facilities for bathing? Were you given any water for cleaning, for washing yourself?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no water was provided except -- there was no water except for the water on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How many hours a day, in a 24-hour period, were you and the other men confined in the room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 24 hours a day, without ever going out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did -- was any medical care provided to any of the persons in that room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Although, as I have already said, one of them had a bullet hole in his leg. He did not receive any medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think this would be a good time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, just before that break we were -- you were telling us what the room was like, what it was like to be inside that prison room. I would now like you, as best you can, to describe the general condition of the other prisoners in the room. And I don't think you need to describe Genov's condition because you've already gone over that. So the other prisoners in the room, people who were there when you arrived, who were already there, how did they appear to you to be physically?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of these persons, as I said, had a bullet hole in his leg and he was in very bad shape because the wound was infested. The others were in a very sorry state, too. Their clothes were also in very bad shape. They were all in very bad shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how did their -- that's their physical state. What was their mental state, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it varied. Some were in very good mental state. Two or three persons were very concerned about what would happen to them. But most people for the most part thought about what would happen to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you, how did you feel while you were in that room for those days and nights?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very scared. I didn't know what would happen, whether they could kill us or let us go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how about your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was also quite scared because I was with him. He was more afraid for my -- on my behalf than as far as he was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You described the clothing of the other prisoners as being dirty or in bad shape. Can you describe what kind of clothing it was and -- That's not a very clear question, but describe what sort of clothing they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were mostly in shirts, T-shirts and trousers. Nobody had any kind of insignia, just your everyday civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who guarded that room you were kept in?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in front of the room or in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, both.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were not allowed or -- to look out of the window. That was the order that we received, so I don't know if anybody stood in front of the basement, but there were guards in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who, if you could tell, had the keys to the room? Could you tell who opened the door to the room when food, water, things like that was brought in?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Shala and another person, a younger person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how many times during the time you were there did you see Shala open the door to the room to bring food or water or cigarettes or whatever?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was mostly present there, but I really don't know whether he would be the one who would open the door. But he was always there, present in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he actually come into the basement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, while you were there did you observe whether any prisoners in that room were beaten?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you know who beat the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three men. They wore black masks over their faces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were those men in any kind of -- well, could you describe the clothing those men wore.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly in camouflage uniforms with the Albanian army insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How often did beatings occur while you were there, approximately?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes it would happen several times per day, but it did also happen every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about at night?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They wouldn't let us sleep. They would wake us up with flashlights, get in and beat people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you describe the beatings that you witnessed in that room.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were all kinds, from punches, kicks with military boots to the head, rifle butts in the kidney area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You said it was two or three soldiers who wore masks who did this. If you can tell, was it the same two or three soldiers or do you mean on different occasions different groups of two or three soldiers would come and beat the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, they wore masks, so I really don't know. But I think it was mostly always the same people who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Shala beat anybody in that room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was your father beaten?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know why you and your father were not beaten?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know the reason for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was Shala present during any of the beatings you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure if he was there every time, but he was present at some of the occasions. He mostly was the one who unlocked the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, at any times when he came -- when Shala came to the prison room, did he speak to you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only asked me on one occasion how I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how was his behaviour to you then? Can you just describe his demeanour and how he was acting towards you while he asked how you were doing.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seemed to me that it was respectful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was anybody in that room singled out? Did anybody receive a more severe beating than the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Genov.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he ever talk -- did you ever talk to Genov at all about these beatings that he was suffering?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. He would moan in pain and at one point he asked me if I could kill him, to strangle him, because he could take the beatings no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologised and I said I couldn't do it. I really couldn't kill him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to talk now with you about the end of this experience in that prison room. How did you come to leave the basement prison room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since they took Genov out and brought him back at one point, they told me to get out. I expected that I would be either killed or beaten. They told me to get out and they told me that they needed to talk to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who -- if you remember who asked you -- who told you to come out and said that they needed to talk to you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a man with a black mask. Shala was also present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did you go out with them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you -- did anybody come with you from the prison or did you leave alone?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point I was alone. I went out alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you could see or tell, how did your father react while they were taking you out of the prison room, Shala and the other soldier?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was very frightened because we all knew what happened to people who were taken out of the basement. So he kept telling them in a scared way to take him instead of me, to kill him rather than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And briefly can you tell the Trial Chamber what you mean by "we all knew what happened to people who were taken out of the basement."

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly they would be beaten and then brought back. That's what happened with Genov, and that's what I expected would happen to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, where were you taken after you were brought out of the room? Where did you go with Shala and the other soldier?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they took me out and I asked them if I could get a breath of fresh air because the stench in the basement was unbearable. They then took me back to the room on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, just so we're clear, we may not need to use any diagrams, is that room on the ground floor you're referring to the same one where you were first brought into when you were brought into the camp when you were questioned?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what happened in the room? Who was there and what were you told?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Shala was there and one or two soldiers. They told me to sit on the floor; I obeyed. They asked me if I was thirsty or hungry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what happened next? What did they -- did they tell you the purpose of why you were being brought out of the room -- out of the basement room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't tell me anything. They just took me to that room and gave me some food and something to drink. They didn't tell me why they had taken me out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you speak to them and say anything to them, to Shala and the other soldier or these soldiers who were present?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understand your question. What do you mean; did I say anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you ask them for anything or to do anything?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I asked them if they could bring my father out of the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened next? Can you tell me the next time you saw your father, how that happened.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think we played a game of chess. He asked me if I played chess and I said, Of course I do. And then I asked him if it would be possible for me to at least see my father and let him know that I was okay. He said I could do that but that it was impossible for my father to be let out at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who is "he" in that answer you just gave? Who did you play chess with and have this conversation with?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. It was Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No need to apologise. Thank you. And could you tell me now how you came to see your father again.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to a toilet that was located a certain distance away from the basement, and I stopped for a moment to talk to my father to let him know that I was okay. And then they decided to let him go, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened with you and your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us back to that room, asked him whether he was thirsty, whether he wanted some coffee. Of course he took the coffee, and we spent a certain period of time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long was the conversation and game of chess with Shala?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not longer than an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say you spent a certain time in the room. Is that still the downstairs room that we've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then what happens? Where are you taken after that? How do you leave that room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Shala or somebody, one of the commanders, decided to move us to the room upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So that would be a room directly above the room you were in at that point?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness P5. I'll ask Mr. Younis if we can go to the upstairs of the main building A1 in Prosecution P6.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, have I ever shown you this display before of this room? And if we can circle, please. Do you remember if I've ever shown you that room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you didn't. You showed me just the downstairs room. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the room that is before you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What room is that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the room on the second floor. That's where we were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, that's the top floor of building A1 in image U008-3669 of Prosecution's Exhibit 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you just briefly tell me how the room was different, if it was different at all, when you were there in 1998. And if we can spin around it once more, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The carpet was different. There was wallpapers and the colour of the mattresses was different and the placement was also different. These pictures were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Who was in the room -- who else was in the room, if anyone, when you were brought into that room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an Albanian, a young man.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was he doing there? What was his status there, if you could tell?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were told later that he had been hiding from the Serb police, because the Serb police allegedly had killed his lambs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was there anybody else in the room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were soldiers present there, but most of the times there were my father, myself, and the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long would you stay in this room? How many days or nights did you spend in this room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we were there for two or three nights. I really am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was there room guarded at all?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The door was locked at all times, but I don't think that there was anybody standing guard in front of the door. There were soldiers downstairs but not upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you ever see Shala while you were in this room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, every day. He came there every day. He brought food.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did he continue to be respectful towards you the way you said he was in your other meetings with him?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was very respectful towards both me and my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to talk a little bit about your interview with the investigator in January 2003. We've already talked about some of the photos he showed you during that interview; photos of some prisoners, an aerial photo, which you marked and labelled. Now, in addition to those which we've talked about, did Investigator Lehtinen show you any other photos, sheets of paper with multiple photos of persons on the same sheet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was the Albanian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, as clearly as you can remember, please tell me what the investigator said to you when he showed you these sheets of paper with photos of several people on them. What did he tell you to do?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me to have a good look and to tell him whether I recognised anyone on the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did he give you any other instructions at all? Just if you remember. If you don't, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Earlier you said -- a few moments ago, when I asked you about these sheets of paper, who were on them, you said: "Yes. There was the Albanian army." What do you mean by "Albanian army" in that answer, if you can clarify a bit.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First he showed me photographs of Genov and Cuk. Then he asked me if I recognised any of those people - among them was the photograph of Shala - and I immediately got an idea that those were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, after you recognised Shala on the photo sheet, did you mark the photo sheet in any way?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I marked it, but I was 100 per cent certain that it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long did it take you to recognise Shala on the photo sheet you were shown?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised him very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did you say to Investigator Lehtinen after you recognised Shala on the photo sheet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told him that it was Shala, that he was one of the soldiers in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd now like to show the witness U003-2190.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Take a moment, sir, and look at that. Do you recognise this photo sheet that's before you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where do you recognise it from?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this sheet for the first time in 2003 when the investigator came to see me and asked me if I was able to recognise any of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who is the man in number -- photo number 8?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is that the same photo you picked out when you were interviewed by Investigator Lehtinen? Is this the same photo sheet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the same piece of paper; it's obviously a copy. But the photograph itself was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Is your signature on this photo sheet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd move to admit that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P83.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to now go back to where we were talking about - I don't have too many more questions for you - your experiences in that upstairs room of the house which you identified for us. Could you hear at all while you were in that room sounds from the outside, from the yard?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
