utterances.text: We could hear people speaking and a shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how often did you hear shots or a shot?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps several times, a few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you allowed outside of that room at all during the time that you stayed there? Were you allowed to leave the room?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: For what purpose?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To go to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness P79, which is under seal, have that placed before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Take a moment and look at that please, sir, and tell me if you've marked the toilets on this diagram and how many toilets you've marked.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are two toilets there on each side. They're marked toilet 1 and toilet 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And which toilet did you use when you were allowed outside the room? The one marked WC1 or the one marked WC2?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I went to WC1 and afterwards they told me to use the other one, WC2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Were you under guard when you would go to and from the toilet or were you allowed to go on your own?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first the guards accompanied us, and afterwards they let us go on our own. When Shala was there with one or two other soldiers only, then he would let us go on our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show an image to the witness now, U008-3672. We can put it on Sanction -- actually, it might be best to leave P79 with him for the moment. And that ERN number I've quoted is from Prosecution Exhibit P6.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at that photo before you now, sir. Tell me if you recognise what's shown there.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is toilet number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And which door is the door to toilet number 2? We could put it on the ELMO and that way you could point to it.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, you're indicating the door towards the back of the photo, facing towards the photo, where one can see the -- that the door is open and can see into the room. In the back of the photo there are two doors; it's the door on the left. Again, that's U008-3672.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, on your way to or from the toilet did you ever speak to anybody?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went by the toilet -- I went by the basement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- where they had first kept us and I asked them how they were doing and how they felt. I asked how Genov was, whether he was there, and they said that they had released him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you know who the two men -- or do you know who you spoke to when you said "they"? Who was that in the basement room where you had been in prison?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell me - I could show you the photos again if you think that would help - which of the prisoners it was you spoke to, or if you could describe them and tell me which one it was.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's all the same to me. Whatever suits you better.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me show you the same -- let me show you the photos. We can do it on Sanction. Could we have U003-2166, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we have U003-2168, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And U003-2169. Do you remember if this was one of the men you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Other than what you've said about how they told you that Genov was released, did they give you any other information about Genov?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just asked how Genov was and they told me that they took him out and that they told them later that they had released them. Now, I wasn't sure whether they actually knew what had happened to Genov or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And just to be clear from your last answer, if I can, "they," the man you've identified, told you that Genov was taken out. And this man told you later that the soldiers or guards had told the Serbs and the prisoners that Genov had been released. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not sure whether the soldiers had told them. But they told me that they found out that Genov had been released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, other than this short conversation that you've just told us about, did you speak -- did you have any other conversations when you made trips to use the toilet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They just asked us how we felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you overhear any conversations from anywhere when you went to use the toilet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard conversations from the room next to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, if we could give the witness P79 again, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Oh, you've got it in front of you. Can you please, by looking at that diagram, tell me where it sounded to you as though those sounds were coming from in relation to WC2.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard to show it on this photograph, but the room on the immediate right when approaching the toilet. That's where the door was and that's where I overheard the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Maybe if we could -- Mr. Younis, if we could show that same photo from P5.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Looking at that image --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Looking at that image in front of you, can you tell us there where sounded to you as though you were hearing conversations coming from, which room. This is U008-3672 which is in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right-hand side, the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for the record, that's the door immediately to the right of the door of the toilet which you've identified for us before?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you hear what was being said at all?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. It was a quiet conversation because obviously someone had said something to them, too, so they didn't dare speak out loud either, but quiet conversations could be overheard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now in general, going back now to your time in the upstairs room, the living room where you were -- spent with your father, how were you treated there in general? Can you describe how you were treated after you were taken out of the prison room.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part they didn't mistreat us, except for one man who mistreated us psychologically rather than physically. But for the most part they respected us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell me what that psychological mistreatment was.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at one moment he came with a pistol and he sat in front of me and my father and he said to my father that he should say goodbye to his son because he would kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how was that man who threatened you dressed? Can you describe him at all?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wore a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he have a mask on?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How did you learn that you were going to be leaving the camp, that you were going to be set free?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one of the men in charge came -- or actually, Shala first said that we should not be afraid, that they would let us go. But then after that, one of the men in charge came up to us and said that they would release us, he wasn't sure when, but he said that they would release us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where did this happen?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upstairs in the house, in that room there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he tell you how you would be released or who you would be released to or how this was going to take place?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't. He just said that they would release us, but that we would first have to make a statement on video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Which one of the men in charge was this who came and told you you would be released and you would have to make a statement on video?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already pointed him out. The same man who is on the Internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for complete clarity, the same man that you drew an arrow towards on the photograph from the Internet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How did he treat you during this conversation when he was speaking to you and your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I would say with respect and in a soldierly fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you -- did you in fact make a statement on a video before you were released?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe that process, where you did that, what you were told to do, and how it was done.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about four or five soldiers in uniform walked in carrying video cameras. They wore berets and most of them had dark glasses on, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. too. They were heavily armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told us to stand in front of the camera and to talk about how they behaved to us and not to dare show any fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did -- did you and your father make these statements at the same time, together, or separately?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, separately. I'm not sure whether he went first or me, but we both made a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you remember, generally speaking, what you said on this statement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we introduced ourselves. We had to say that they fed us regularly and how they behaved towards us, that we were not mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long did this take?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to start all over again several times. They were telling me to calm down, not to show any fear, but I did not know what would happen after this statement so I was a bit afraid of making that statement. They said that if I showed fear one more time, they would kill us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, please tell the Chamber as best you remember how you actually left the camp. How long was it after this statement was completed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was the day after that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how did you leave? Tell us how you left, where you were brought, who took you where, how you came to actually leave the camp.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a Jeep parked in the yard. They put black blindfolds over our eyes and they drove us somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were there any markings or insignia on the Jeep, anything special about it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long does this journey in the car take -- in the Jeep, sorry?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happens?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We entered a small town where there were quite a few people in the centre. Most of them were armed, and it was all men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you know which town you were in?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when were the blindfolds -- when had the blindfolds been taken off?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as we got out to the main road, the asphalt road, before we entered town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened in the town after the Jeep stopped?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men, these terrorists, got out and they crossed the street. On the other side of the street a Jeep was parked of the UN -- of UNICEF, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What organisation was the Jeep from?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think UNICEF.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Albanians entered a place that looked like a village restaurant. Then they walked out, together with some people from UNICEF, and they transferred us to their Jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then where did you go, what happened?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They drove us out of that town, in those Jeeps. I'm not sure where, but we reached a Serb police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when did you meet up with your mother again? The first time after being released, I'm speaking about.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three days after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where was it in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the apartment of a lady who had sent us to Kosovo; Ruzica Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who was she? What was her position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that she was in charge of the Kosovo Red Cross, the Red Cross for the province of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And -- and did you find out when you met your mother what she'd been doing during the time that you'd been missing, held captive?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She stated in public, on television, what had happened and where they kidnapped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, when you were with Ruzica Simic at her house, did you meet with anybody else? And I'm talking about people other than family members, other than people working for the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at one point in time a man came and asked us whether we recognised a person; I don't know exactly who it was. I don't know whether it was his brother or his relative. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of this man or where he was from?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he show you anything?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were able to give -- to answer any of his questions or not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did you tell him?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he asked me whether I recognised a person in a picture. I'm not sure who that was, but I do remember that that person was with us in that basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just to be very clear, you remember that the person was with you in the basement in the camp you'd just been released from?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you remember anything else about the person who had been -- who he was seeking information about who had been in the basement with you in the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I don't have any more questions for you at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Khan, how are we situated?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, as I mentioned this morning, there is the issue regarding the further investigations. Perhaps my friend Mr. Guy-Smith can continue for the time being. I have been told by my friend Mr. Black, and Mr. Nicholls, they've made some efforts and it seems that the web site itself was referred to by a newspaper or some other Internet site back in 1997, I think it was -- or I don't remember the date --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What we showed you, just to be clear, is in May 1993 there was a link to the site and a description of it -- sorry, in May 1999 there was a link to the site and a description of the site on the Business Week web site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do I take it that you would prefer to delay for a time, Mr. Khan, your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes, in candour, I don't know -- this is out of a matter of prudence. I don't know if by Monday we will be able to obtain the necessary information but we won't seek to delay it beyond on Monday. I know it is available. There are experts out there who are very expensive, hundreds of pounds, I'm told, per hour, that have the expertise in going back to web sites and finding out what was on a web site at a particular time. But I think it's a matter that we should at least try and look into, if not by these expensive experts, by us perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll keep looking at it. But my understanding primarily of what we've established is that the web site was in operation in 1999, so I think that narrows down any possible missing information quite a bit just relating specifically to any photos. So all cross-examination other than that one question I think could take place. And if there is, we could wait until Monday, and if there's more on that single specific issue, that's fine, but there may not be an answer or there may not need to be any further cross, depending on what's found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to keep jumping up. I don't want to delay matters. I have stated the case quite squarely. There are other options, of course. If my learned friend Mr. Guy-Smith finishes with plenty of time to spare, one option, of course, is that I continue and if investigations come to light that -- well, if we have the funds to make these investigations at first instance there are other avenues available to us. But at the moment I thought out of prudence I should make attempts to look into this further because, of course, it could be somewhat important for my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith, you've been named a couple of times. Do you have a view whether you would be prepared to proceed now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I -- I was going to suggest that perhaps a solution to the problem would be that I do proceed now. I may well have some questions with regard to the Internet site; however, I believe that I may be able to ask those questions and, in the event some of the concerns that have been voiced do come into play, there will be a mechanism whereby I will be either able to remedy or recall, if need be, any witnesses for purposes of cross-examinations. But if I have the permission of my colleague here, I'm more than happy to stand at the podium for a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you would proceed then, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I represent Haradin Bala. He is one of the individuals who is presently sitting at this trial. I would like to ask you questions in a number of different areas. In the event you have any difficulties understanding any of my questions, please do let me know. Okay?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This entire incident that occurred to you is something that caused you then a great deal of distress. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that it is an incident that you have attempted to, to the best of your ability, erase from your mind?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Things like these cannot be forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm not getting sound for some reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand your answer. My question is: It's something you've tried to do?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's something that in fact you have been reluctant to speak of?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It is a conversation that you have not had with your family over these number of years since the incident. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And it is something that, although you experienced this with your father, it's something that you and your father have not spoken of since it occurred. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we did speak a few times, but not any lengthy conversations. We perhaps exchanged just a few words about what the house looked like, what the yard looked like, but not in any great detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that you perhaps did speak a few times, could you tell the Tribunal when these conversations were. And perhaps if it's of any help to you, were these conversations before you surfed on the 'net in 1999 or after you surfed on the 'net?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before and after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you surfed on the 'net in 1999 because of your interest in what was going on in Kosovo, sir, did you have an opportunity to speak to any investigators about your experiences?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Do you mean an investigator from here or from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, let's start with from Serbia. I take it that you had an opportunity to speak to an investigator from Serbia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in 1999. We did not have any conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you ever present when your father had an opportunity to speak to an investigator from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I'm able to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that your father spoke with an investigator from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before 1999 is what my question refers to for the moment, before you started surfing on the 'net.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The conversations took place after our release from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many conversations did you have after you were released from the camp with the Serbian investigators?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps two or three times, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the first of those conversations, was that a conversation that you had with your father present?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have any information that would assist you with regard to whether or not your father was present at the first conversations you had with the Serbian authorities? And by that I mean any notes, any diaries, or journals.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall the Serbian authority speaking with your father after you were released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. It was at the Red Cross in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And were you present at the time that your father was having a conversation with Serbian authorities after you were released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How long did that conversation last, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many people were present in that conversation, apart from yourself and your father, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ruzica Simic, among others. There were three or four other people. I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, could you tell us, those three or four other people, were they men or women?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you tell us as you sit here today whether they were dressed in civilian clothes or wearing uniforms of any sort.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in civilian clothes, in suits.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that there was perhaps two or three conversations that you had with Serbian authorities. And what I'd like to discuss with you at this moment is with regard to the other conversations that were had with Serbian authorities. In each of those conversations were you sitting, listening to your father discuss what had happened at the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first time it happened as soon as we walked into the Red Cross building. We sat down and we discussed what had happened. And the second time was at the table where there were several other persons present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "we discussed," is it fair to say that both you and your father were involved in a question/answer discussion with some members of the police, the Serbian police, that is?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my father spoke for most of the time. They just asked me how I felt at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So apart from asking you that one specific question, which is how you felt, you did not give any further information to the Serbian police Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with regard to your experiences at the camp. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who you saw at the camp. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who you spoke to at the camp. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What food you ate at the camp. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Where you stayed at the camp. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The identification of any individuals that you met at the camp. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The clothes that any individuals were wearing at the camp. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The movements that you, you personally, were involved in in the camp, and by that I mean from the area that you've called the basement to the area that you've called the house. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We didn't discuss anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Nor did you speak of, with the Serbian police, the conversations you had with the individual you believed to be Shala. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You're clear about not speaking with the Serbian police with regard to identification of any individuals. Right? That's something you're clear you did not do.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, you certainly spoke to the Serbian police at the time that you were meeting with your father, with them, about playing chess with Shala, did you not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that with regard to the other matters that you've testified, both today and yesterday about, you do not remember speaking to the Serbian police shortly after you were released from the camp about any of those matters, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversations -- there were conversations about the identification. But I don't remember any more than that because I was in a state of shock.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "there were conversations about identifications," which you don't remember because of your understandable state, do you recall whether or not the Serbian police who you were speaking with were taking notes?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us as you sit here today about how long the total number of hours were spent in your interviews with the Serbian police shortly after you left the camp.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour -- an hour or two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "an hour or two hours," does that take into account all of the conversations? Because as I understand your testimony, there were two or three conversations.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember as you sit here today how long after the first time you met with the Serbian police you had the second interview with them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the first day after we were released there was a talk at the Red Cross. And then the day after, there was this other conversation with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that the sum total of interviews that you and your father had with the Serbian police after you were released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any interviews with Serbian police after you were released from the camp anywhere outside of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the police checkpoint at the entrance to Pristina. I think that this part belonged to the Serb police. They stopped the UNICEF Jeep and asked us who we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At that time did you have an interview with them about your experiences at the camp, with the Serbian police at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that the only question was who we were and where we were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from the three times you have just mentioned, did you have any other contact with Serbian authorities before you left Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent the few days in the home of Ruzica Simic, so we were in contact with her and with the Red Cross people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were in contact with Ruzica Simic, did you tell her about your experiences at the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she asked us how it was down there. We explained to her how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to distinguish, if I can, for a minute between what you did and what your father did. When there were discussions with Ruzica Simic, was it your father talking to her and you listening in the same fashion that this was occurring when you were speaking with the Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the conversation with them was mostly about how we felt down there and -- in fact, the conversation with her, she only wanted to know whether we had been maltreated down there. It wasn't so much about the facts, what had happened, when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What I'm trying to understand is whether or not you had a one-to-one conversation with this woman. Did you speak to her by yourself without your father present?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And would it be fair to say that in the conversations she was having, trying to make a determination of how you were treated, she was having a conversation with your father. You were present; true?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were listening to what was being said. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And sometimes you would add information. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But the lion's share, the conversation that was occurring was a conversation that was occurring between Ruzica Simic and your father; right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is exactly the same thing that occurred when you were speaking with the Serbian police. Correct? And by that I mean the Serbian police were speaking with your father. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were present?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Listening in and on occasion adding information?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I want to make sure because I don't want to leave Kosovo without having covered all of the interviews your father was in when you were present. Have we missed any?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before moving to your new home - and please be aware of the fact that I have no interest in knowing where that home is - in 1998, shortly after left the camp, did you receive counselling because of your shock?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I refused counselling. My father accepted medical help, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When your father accepted medical help, did you accompany him?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Between the time that you left the camp and today's date, have you had any conversations with any police authorities from Belgrade? And by "you," I mean you, sir, not you and your father.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again, a question that I asked you previously: Do you have any kind of note, journal, or diary that would assist you in remembering whether or not you have had any conversations with any police authorities from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, sorry, but as he says, since he's asked it before and got an answer before, I don't see the need to re-ask it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's a distinct question whether, for example, there might be any diary that could be referred to. Please carry on, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it. I did not keep any sort of diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you first -- before you came to your new home, did you have any discussion with any embassy authorities concerning your time at the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You then came to your new home. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Between the time that you left Kosovo travelling however long that took you, and I'm once again not asking for that information, during the period of your travels before arriving at your new home, did you have conversations with any individuals or representatives of any investigative organisations concerning your experiences at the camp, other than the ones you have so far mentioned to us?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you arrived at your new home, that was in the year 1998, was it not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And for the balance of that year, from September through December of 1998, during that period of time, did you and your father have any of the brief discussions you told us about earlier?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the conversations between us two or with any authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just between you two.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were conversations, just a few of them, how we felt after all that. Nothing more than that was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Moving to the year 1999, did you continue to live in your new home. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And it's the year 1999 that you have some interest in what's going on in Kosovo, such an interest that you begin to look on the Internet for information concerning Kosovo. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Even before that we had an interest but not as much as we did after we finally got a computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you got the computer, while you were in your new home, were you met -- did you meet - by that I mean you and your father for the moment - with any journalists, newspaper reporters, television reporters concerning your experiences?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that it's important, if you don't mind terribly, either speaking up a bit or moving closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no conversations between my father, myself, and any journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did your father have any conversation with any journalists between the time that you first arrived at your new home and the time that you obtained the computer?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a local journalist. He only asked us about the situation in Kosovo, what was going on in Kosovo and what we thought about all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was that before you got the computer or after you obtained the computer?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure -- I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you participated in that interview also, I take it from the answer that you've just given, which is: "He only asked us about the situation in Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you add information to what your father was saying in the same fashion that you had done when speaking with the Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps we should go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from the contact you had with this local television station in -- I believe we are still in the year 1998 and 1999 before you obtained your computer, did you have any contact with any other individuals concerning your experiences at the camp?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it that you continued to refuse any counselling from the time you reached your new home up until the time you obtained your computer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember when you obtained this new computer?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in 1999. I'm not sure of the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, as I understand -- understood your testimony, when you first arrived at your new home, you were in school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not immediately. I completed high school in Kosovo, and after we moved away I continued my education a year later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you obtained this computer before you began your education, and by that I mean continued your education at your new home?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you continued your education, do you recall whether the education that you continued was in the fall of 1999?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So sometime between, perhaps, January and September of 1999 is when your family obtained this computer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before obtaining this computer, you were familiar, were you not, with surfing the 'net, as it's called in certain parlance?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And at some point in time I take it - once again, please do correct me if I'm wrong - either you or you and your father decided to find out what was going on in Kosovo, and as a result of that decision, began looking for information on the Internet. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was it you who found this particular web site, www.kosovo.com?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you found this particular web site, is that something you found by hunting around or was that a web site that you had been referred to by someone else?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I searched for it. I typed the word "Kosovo" in the search engine and that's the first site that came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you use Google?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yahoo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think Google is better. When you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told Google did not exist in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have to think about that. I take the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you got this information and you found this particular web site, you spent a fair amount of time looking at this web site, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that in your estimation this web site is a balanced web site, a web site that gives all sides of the picture on what's going on in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a web site that is mainly related to Serb Orthodox churches in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many times do you think you personally visited this web site - and by that I mean reviewed and looked at the information on it - between the time you first got a computer and the time you started your studies?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe once or twice a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you visited this web site, did you spend a fair amount of time on the web site? And by that I mean could you tell us how many links you may have looked on the web site, what information you pulled off of this web site then?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part it was daily news, what was going on in Kosovo at the moment, and there were pictures from Kosovo as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you looked at this web site, were you looking at it always by yourself or was this a family affair where your father, your mother, and your brother would participate in obtaining information about something that was important to you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mostly did my own searches and looked at what was going on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall as you sit here today commenting -- commenting to your father when you found something of interest?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall how many times you did that? And once again I'm talking about between the time that you first got the computer up to the time that you began your studies in the fall.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know how many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: More than a handful?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And after you did this with your father, for example, you saw something that was noteworthy, you and he talked about Kosovo. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in some of those conversations you and he talked about how lucky you felt having survived the experiences that you'd had. Right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in some of those conversations you talked about and remembered some of the things that you'd seen, that you'd heard, that you'd felt while you were at that camp. True?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You start your education in the fall of 1999. And from the fall until the end of that year, 1999, December that would be, obviously, I take it you continued in the same fashion to look at this particular web site. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but with less interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "with less interest," do you mean that you found the subject growing old and that there were new challenges in your life then? Or do you mean that you were looking at it less frequently?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment I was more interested in things that had to do with my education rather than what was going on in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us about how many times, if you could - and I understand it's but an estimate - how many times a week you would look at the web site during that period of your life.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps once or twice a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during that period of your life, that once or twice a week that you would look at the web site, do you recall whether during that period of time there was anything noteworthy that you recognised that you discussed with your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were pictures there of Albanian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you saw those pictures of Albanian soldiers, that's something that you discussed with your father. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's something you discussed with your father on more than one occasion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, in the year 2000 - and rather than break the year up by six months or so, I'll just do the entire year of 2000 - in the year 2000 you continued with your studies. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during that period of time, in the year 2000, was your family contacted by any investigators concerning themselves with what had occurred in 1998?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And just to be sure. For the last part of 1999 I take your answer to be the same; that your family was not contacted, as far as you can remember, by any investigators concerning these incidents?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 2001, by this point in time, if I understood your previous testimony correctly, you are probably not frequenting this web site as much?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Checking it on occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And of course any time that anything was noteworthy, that was something that you and your father would discuss. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I've noticed - and I do apologise - that I haven't mentioned your brother with regard to these discussions. So very quickly, when you notice something noteworthy on the Internet, did you have discussions with your brother? And what I'm talking about is from the period of time when you first obtained the computer until the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not as much as I did with my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And how about with your mother? Would the same answer be true for your mother?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And by that -- by yes, you did but not as much with your father?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from the one web site that you've mentioned, the www.kosovo.com, did you visit any other web sites that dealt with matters pertaining to Kosovo during this period of time, and by that I mean from the time you first got the computer through the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the press agencies from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "just the press agencies from Serbia," I don't think there's any trouble identifying those in open court, is there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you identify those for us, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly B92, www.b92.com. It all depends. I mostly went to Serbian sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it your answers would be the same with regard to the kinds of discussions you had with your father about those sites that we've discussed when it comes to the discussions you had with your father about the www.kosovo.com site. Correct? When you found something noteworthy, you two would have a discussion about it, and you would in those discussions, of course, discuss matters that were quite unique to you and to your father.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The years 2001 and 2002 I take it are pretty much the same. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And by "pretty much the same," you were periodically checking in, seeing what was going on, digesting information and commenting on it when appropriate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When is the first time that you became aware of interest by investigators for the ICTY in you and your father's story?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in late 2002. They contacted my grandmother and asked her if they could speak to us in this regard. She later gave them our address, and then they came to see us in January.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Without telling us where your grandmother is presently residing, when your grandmother received the information that investigators from the ICTY were interested in talking to you, she contacted your father or your mother. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When your grandmother contacted one of your parents, that of course caused a discussion about what had happened to you, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the discussion mostly centred on whether we were willing or not to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Of course. That was a discussion that was actually in many senses of a fair amount of importance to both you and your father. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the two of you, in trying to make a determination of how you were going to proceed, discussed what had happened and whether or not you wished to deal with that again.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember how you were contacted by the investigator? Was that by phone or by letter?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By telephone. I was not present at that time because I was at college, but my mother told me that they had called, that somebody from the Tribunal here had called.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And then arrangements were made, I take it, for you to meet with this person?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, before you met with this individual -- and that individual was Ole Lehtinen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And no one else?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and also an interpreter for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to object on relevance at that point. It's got nothing to do with any issue in dispute and it's not a proper topic for cross, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't have any -- I don't have any need to plough the ground. It's of some interest but not great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you actually met with this investigator, Mr. Lehtinen, did you talk to him - and by that I mean you personally - talk to him on the telephone with regard to what the subject matter of his interest in you was?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not speak to him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you obtain information from your father regarding what Mr. Lehtinen wanted to discuss with you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What did your father tell you Mr. Lehtinen wanted to discuss with you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me that they mostly want to talk to us about what had happened in Kosovo and whether it would be -- if it would be okay, that he would like to come and see us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After a discussion with your father, the two of you agreed that it would be okay for him to come to see you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAKRAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a lengthy discussion between the two of us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am about to enter into a relatively long and new area. I know that it's still --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. I think that would be a very appropriate time to break. Sir, we will be having to finish for today now, but we will resume on Monday. So your evidence will continue then. We will adjourn now to resume on Monday at 2.15. Perhaps before I do, do I understand, Mr. Guy-Smith, that this document is now no longer required?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Many years ago I was told that discretion is the better part of valour, so if it does not take up too much room, Your Honour, if for but a brief number of days it could be retained, I would appreciate it. I think it may well not be required, but exercising a bit more caution ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can never interfere with caution on the part of counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of December, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
